sentiment.label: risk_on
sentiment.reason_it: Il VIX a 17.31 (‑6,13%) indica un mercato difensivo limitato; il S&P 500 è a 7.712,57 (+0,28%) e il DXY a 101,79 (+0,05%), segnando stabilità del dollaro. Il Brent sale a $110,25 (+1,34%) sostenendo l'appeal dei risk assets, mentre l'oro rimane quasi invariato a $4.143,90/oz (+0,03%). La compressione del TLT (+0,84%) suggerisce tassi stabili, coerente con il range Fed 3,75‑4,00% e il DFR BCE al 2,50%. Questi dati convergono verso un contesto di risk‑on moderato.
sentiment.reason_en: The VIX at 17.31 (‑6.13%) points to limited defensive positioning; the S&P 500 stands at 7,712.57 (+0.28%) and the DXY at 101.79 (+0.05%), indicating dollar stability. Brent climbs to $110.25 (+1.34%) supporting risk assets, while gold is flat at $4,143.90/oz (+0.03%). TLT’s modest rise (+0.84%) signals stable rates, in line with the Fed range 3.75‑4.00% and ECB DFR at 2.50%. These data converge toward a moderate risk‑on environment.

market_impact_summary.it: Equity europee mostrano pressione: STOXX 600 a 63,36 (‑0,85%) e FTSE MIB a 49.071 (‑0,03%). Al contrario, i mercati USA rimangono rialzisti (+0,28% S&P). Il Brent in spike (+1,34%) alimenta inflazione ma favorisce le commodity; l'oro resta stabile (+0,03%). Il TLT in salita (+0,84%) indica tassi contenuti, mentre il DXY leggermente più forte (+0,05%) pesa su asset a rischio. In sintesi, il mix di equity US positive, commodity in crescita e tassi stabili genera un impatto netto bullish.
market_impact_summary.en: European equities are under pressure: STOXX 600 at 63.36 (‑0.85%) and FTSE MIB at 49,071 (‑0.03%). Conversely, US markets stay positive (+0.28% S&P). Brent spikes (+1.34%) fuels commodity appeal; gold is flat (+0.03%). TLT rises (+0.84%) signalling contained rates, while the DXY’s slight gain (+0.05%) dampens risk assets. Overall, the blend of strong US equity, rising commodities and stable rates yields a net bullish market impact.

articles.title: Guns, Growth, and the German Reinvention of Military Keynesianism
articles.snippet: In March 2025, Germany did more than loosen a fiscal rule. It fused two national emergencies — a deteriorating European security order and a deteriorating industrial model — into a single constitutional bargain. The reform de facto exempted German defense expenditure from any domestic budgetary ceiling — as the German Bundesbank itself has acknowledged — and enabled a military expansion of extraordinary proportions.
